content: A lacteal is a specialized lymphatic capillary located within the villi of the small intestine, responsible for the absorption of dietary fats. The absorbed fats combine with lymph within the lacteals, forming a milky fluid known as chyle. Individual lacteals converge to form larger lymphatic vessels, which transport the chyle to the thoracic duct. The thoracic duct subsequently empties its contents into the left subclavian vein, introducing the fats into the bloodstream. Once in the bloodstream, these fats can undergo conversion in the liver into lipoproteins, such as high-density lipoproteins (HDL), low-density lipoproteins (LDL), or very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDL). Alternatively, the fats can be transported to various tissues throughout the body, where they are stored in adipose cells in the form of triglycerides.
